agent_answer_excerpt:
## Scope first

The Knowledge Plane governs a **sales-side P&L only** — revenue, COGS, gross profit, discounts. There are no governed concepts for operating expenses, net income, cash, assets or liabilities, so "financial situation" below the gross-profit line isn't answerable from this data. Everything under is gross-profit level, in USD.

## 2023 — the governed picture

| | 2023 | vs 2022 |
|---|---|---|
| Gross revenue (list) | $333.43M | −28.5% |
| Discounts | $19.75M (5.92%) | rate flat |
| **Net revenue** (kp:TotalSales) | **$313.68M** | **−28.5%** |
| COGS (kp:TotalCost) | $138.13M | −28.6% |
| **Gross profit** (kp:Margin) | **$175.55M** | **−28.3%** |
| Gross margin % | 55.97% | +0.10 pt |
| Orders | 159,695 | −17.6% |
| Avg selling price | $259.93 | −13.1% |
| Markup % | 127.1% | +0.5 pt |

**The read:** 2023 was a sharp top-line contraction that left profitability structurally intact. Margin held at 55.97% and the discount rate was unchanged at 5.92% — the shortfall is entirely volume and mix, not pricing or markdown pressure. Orders fell 17.6% and average order value fell on top of that.
